title: The index isn't the economy
summary: The market can rise while things feel weak. A few giant companies can carry the whole index.

cards.headline: Index isn't the economy
cards.body: A stock index tracks a basket of companies, weighted mostly by size. It can rise while the economy feels weak, because a few giant firms can carry it. The index measures those companies' prices, not jobs, wages, or growth on the ground.

cards.headline: Weighted by size
cards.body: Cap-weighted indexes give the biggest companies the most sway. When a handful of large firms rally, the whole index can look healthy even if most of its members are flat or falling. "The market is up" can hide a lot underneath.

cards.title: The takeaway
cards.summary: An index reflects its members' prices, weighted by size, not the broader economy.
bullets: A few giants can move a cap-weighted index.
A green index with mixed members is common.
"The economy" and "the market" are different gauges.
